One thing I often hear when I'm talking to people who question the existence of magick, the occult, and supernatural phenomena, is 'But you don't really believe that you can do x/y/z'. And who can blame them? From a purely materialistic viewpoint it makes sense that magick is impossible, since, if your consciousness is trapped inside your skull, how would you go about influencing external objective reality? But that's where the flaw in their thinking becomes apparent. Their worldview is either a purely materialistic, where there is only matter and no mind, or a realistic, where there is a mind/matter duality. Just to clear things up, I use the words mind and consciousness interchangeably. But there is a third option: Idealism. Idealism states that the only thing in existence is consciousness, and it is this consciousness that is the groundwork of reality, as opposed to materialism, where it's particles. This opens up a whole new perspective: If our bodies are in consciousness, instead of consciousness in our bodies, supernatural phenomena, the occult and magick suddenly don't sound as illogical and impossible as before. They are a natural part of our world. Because if you think about it, since everything is consciousness, your aren't 'trapped' inside your head anymore. You can influence the 'external' world with your mind alone.

Of course, you can't just go, fly through the sky and change the color of the sun, because you have to remember, you are just a tiny little speck in this gigantic stream of consciousness that is reality! This metaphysical worldview really helped me lay down the foundation upon which to build my understanding of magick. Especially, because it is very much the most logical one!
